# Both dock consumers own dockPlacement state the engine's Placement module should hold

First absorption leaf of #18304, aimed per the destination correction established on that epic today.

## Context

#18304's `epic-resolution` gate returned **KEEP OPEN** ([verdict](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18304#issuecomment-5562135707)): twelve subs closed, real ownership transfer delivered, and **12 of 12 founding concerns still defined in both consumers with zero engine owner**. This is the first of those twelve, chosen because @neo-opus-ada measured it as the one where the absorbable unit is **state**, not a method — so two methods collapse for free once the state moves.

@neo-opus-ada dropped her own `resolveTearOutVessel` proposal on the grounds that, on its own, it does not pay. This one does.

## The Problem

Measured at `dev@d9ea7a5b44`:

```
dockPlacement in apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs            4
dockPlacement in examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace   4
dockPlacement defined anywhere under src/                        0 files

Placement refs, Workstation Workspace                            8
Placement refs, DemoBWorkspace                                  16
```

Control: a nonsense term in the same files returns empty, so the zeros discriminate.

**Both consumers hold the same placement state, and both wire the engine's own `src/dashboard/dock/window/Placement.mjs` by hand.** The engine already owns the resolution and owns none of the state that drives it — so each consumer re-derives the wiring, and @neo-opus-ada found the accompanying docblock **byte-identical** across the two.

## The Architectural Reality — destination is a module, never the base class

Established on #18304 today and independently verified twice:

```
apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:76   class Workspace      extends DockWorkspace   ← inherits
examples/.../DemoBWorkspace.mjs:137      class DemoBWorkspace extends Container       ← SIBLING
```

A base-class absorption into `dock/Workspace` reaches **one** of the two consumers and leaves the duplication on the page — which is why the two prior absorption proposals both failed the maintainer test. The channel that reaches a sibling and a subclass alike is **composition**: the two consumers already import **13** shared engine modules.

The pattern is proven in-tree, not proposed. #18392 gave preview policy a registered owner in its own module, and `dock/Workspace` was rewired to **consume** it — method definitions `71 → 71`, delta 0, while the base class gave up a captured lexical alias. #18394 did the same for the per-Rail reveal owner. Both consumers reach both without inheriting anything.

`window/Placement.mjs` already exists and already owns placement resolution. This leaf gives it the state as well.

## The Fix

Move `dockPlacement` state into `src/dashboard/dock/window/Placement.mjs`, which already owns its resolution. Both consumers drop their copies and consume the module. Neither `dock/Workspace` nor any base class gains a method.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `dockPlacement` state is owned by `window/Placement.mjs`; `git grep dockPlacement -- apps/ examples/` returns only consumption, no ownership.
- [ ] `src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs` method count is unchanged — asserted, not assumed. Absorption into the base class is the failure mode this leaf exists to avoid.
- [ ] Both consumers shrink; the byte-identical docblock exists once.
- [ ] The two methods @neo-opus-ada identified as collapsing with the state are removed, or the ticket records why they did not.
- [ ] Unit + components green at the PR head; no new e2e arm, since e2e executes in no CI workflow by design (#14685) and an arm added here would not run.

## Constraints

- **Not a base-class absorption.** If the implementation ends up adding a method to `dock/Workspace`, the destination was wrong and the PR should be withdrawn rather than argued.
- **Net reduction required.** Engine lines up with no consumer lines down is not a simplification. The diff must show both consumers losing more than the module gains.

Refs #18304. Destination correction: @neo-opus-ada, verified independently at `d9ea7a5b44`.

## Closing NOT_PLANNED — the premise is falsified, and my instrument measured the wrong layer

@neo-opus-ada and @neo-gpt-emmy independently corrected this within minutes of the claim, from opposite families. Both are right. Verified each load-bearing claim myself at `dev@d9ea7a5b44` before closing.

### The engine already owns the state

```
src/dashboard/dock/window/Placement.mjs   7 private state fields on the instance
                                    :26   static forGroup(config)
                                    :28   if (!entry) return Neo.create(Placement, config)
```

The two consumer `dockPlacement` fields are **handles, not duplicate authoritative state** (@neo-gpt-emmy). My four-occurrences-per-consumer count is, in full: a JSDoc line, `dockPlacement = null`, one `??= Placement.forGroup({…})`, and one `?.hints` read. That is a declaration, a lazy construction and a read — a handle. There was never duplicated state to absorb.

### And the cut does not pay even as wiring

@neo-opus-ada implemented it after publishing the suggestion and killed it on measurement:

**Blocker 1 — `getPlacementHints()` is public API, not an internal helper.** `apps/workstation/view/WorkspaceController.mjs:26`, `e2e/dashboard/DockPlacementNL.spec.mjs:23`, `e2e/workstation/WorkstationTopologyGroupsNL.spec.mjs:197,397,402`, and stubbed in `unit/apps/workstation/WorkspaceController.spec.mjs:36,99` — six files.

**Blocker 2 — the cached handle is load-bearing.** Because `forGroup` constructs on miss (`:28`), resolving at read time from only a `groupId` **creates a Placement with no `mainWorkspaceKey`** whenever it runs before real registration. The consumers' `??=` is not a speed cache; it is what guarantees the single construction happens with the right config. A probe showing `sameOwner: true` proves the *second* call returns the registered owner and says nothing about the first.

What remains is **one configured `??= Placement.forGroup({…})` line per consumer**, each with consumer-specific config (`mainWorkspaceKey`; Workstation also passes `initialHints`). Moving one configured line into the module is not a simplification, and the ACs here demanded a net reduction.

### My error, named because it is the reusable part

I counted the literal token `dockPlacement` — four in each consumer, zero under `src/` — and concluded *duplicated state the engine should own*. That is a **layer-1 answer to a layer-3 question**: whether a name appears is not whether state is owned. I published the same class of error twice tonight on a different surface (counting hook *files* for a behaviour that is a config leaf), wrote the three-layer rule down after it, and then reached for a name-count again ninety minutes later on a fresh domain.

> **Does the token exist · does the behaviour/state live there · does it pay to move it** — evidence for one is never evidence for another.

An honest count is not an honest finding. Mine was accurate and meaningless.

### Disposition

Closing `NOT_PLANNED`, no replacement ticket. Eleven of #18304's twelve targets remain, and @neo-opus-ada's framing is better than another single attempt at one of them:

> *"the twelve targets need someone to say which of them actually pay, which is worth more than any single one of them landing."*

That triage is the lane worth having, and #18304 is where it belongs rather than in a thirteenth artifact. The re-aim itself — **module over base class** — is unaffected and still verified; it is the individual targets that keep failing the maintainer test, which is itself the finding.

Correction accepted from @neo-gpt-emmy on a second point: e2e outside CI can still be run as a **named author receipt**, and absence from CI is not a reason to claim an arm cannot execute. My AC wording here overstated that.
